message: Interface and prerequisites for the Git segment, early as you asked. Segment: bend2/scripts/git-acceptance.sh. Invocation: 'sh bend2/scripts/git-acceptance.sh [all|landing-publishing|target-move|conflict-recovery]' - no argument means all three; each name runs only that scenario, so your driver can call them as separate steps. Exit: 0 only when every selected scenario is green; non-zero on the first failure with the failing step named. Stdout: the real evidence of each step (each landing/push answer verbatim, the gate check's own line when the target moves, the ls-remote read-back, the worker reports) and per scenario a line 'git acceptance: <name> ok', ending with 'bend2 git acceptance: green - N scenarios, 0 failures' or 'FAILED - <names>'. Prerequisites, all checked by the script with a named refusal: bend 2.0.25 (BEND, else .bend/bin/bend, else node_modules/.bend/bin/bend; the script builds the coordinator the way check-native.sh does), clang and sqlite3 headers, git, the OMP CLI (BATON_OMP, default /opt/homebrew/bin/omp) with usable credentials in the inherited HOME, and a native model route that is actually available (BATON_WORKER_MODEL, default deepseek/deepseek-flash). No push and no network remote: each scenario declares a scratch bare repository as the remote, and the coordinator pushes to that. Each scenario runs in its own mktemp directory under /tmp and leaves it in place, printing the path, so a failure can be inspected. Duration: about a minute per scenario with three real worker turns each (mine are ~10 s per turn); all three under five minutes. Scenarios: landing-publishing (one real worker commits, the gated landing lands it, the coordinator pushes the landed target and git ls-remote reads the advertised ref back, then a remote moved independently makes the next push answer rejected); target-move (two real workers from one target, the target moves under the second landing while its gate runs, it lands on top of the first with both changes); conflict-recovery (two real workers on one file, the second landing conflicts, the root guides it with a coordinator message, the worker's resumed turn rebases and resolves, and the revised branch lands). I am writing it now and will send you the tip when it is green.
